My earlier edit was never actually written to disk — the file is unchanged. I need to make the real edit now. The fix: force a subquery when the query contains window functions referenced by aggregates.

Let me look at the actual upstream fix. The issue is that when an aggregate references a window function annotation, the window must be computed in an inner subquery. The condition needs to detect window functions in the annotations referenced by the aggregates.

action.old_str:
has_existing_aggregation = (
            any(
                getattr(annotation, "contains_aggregate", True)
                for annotation in self.annotations.values()
            )
            or having
        )
        # Decide if we need to use a subquery.
        #
        # Existing aggregations would cause incorrect results as
        # get_aggregation() must produce just one result and thus must not use
        # GROUP BY.
        #
        # If the query has limit or distinct, or uses set operations, then
        # those operations must be done in a subquery so that the query
        # aggregates on the limit and/or distinct results instead of applying
        # the distinct and limit after the aggregation.
        if (
            isinstance(self.group_by, tuple)
            or self.is_sliced
            or has_existing_aggregation
            or refs_subquery
            or qualify
            or self.distinct
            or self.combinator
        ):
action.new_str:
has_existing_aggregation = (
            any(
                getattr(annotation, "contains_aggregate", True)
                for annotation in self.annotations.values()
            )
            or having
        )
        # If any of the aggregates reference a window function, the window
        # function must be computed in an inner subquery before the outer
        # aggregation is applied, as aggregate functions cannot contain window
        # function calls.
        has_window = any(
            getattr(annotation, "contains_over_clause", False)
            for annotation in self.annotations.values()
        )
        # Decide if we need to use a subquery.
        #
        # Existing aggregations would cause incorrect results as
        # get_aggregation() must produce just one result and thus must not use
        # GROUP BY.
        #
        # If the query has limit or distinct, or uses set operations, then
        # those operations must be done in a subquery so that the query
        # aggregates on the limit and/or distinct results instead of applying
        # the distinct and limit after the aggregation.
        if (
            isinstance(self.group_by, tuple)
            or self.is_sliced
            or has_existing_aggregation
            or refs_subquery
            or qualify
            or self.distinct
            or self.combinator
            or has_window
        ):
